Amy — thanks for the clear list. Below is a compact cheat-sheet and a simple decision tree you can paste into your procurement thread. Happy to hop on a 20-min call with your procurement lead if helpful.

Quick pricing options (pros/cons):
- Annual committed (prepaid) — lowest unit cost, requires procurement/legal comfort with 12+ mo commitment, simplest for AWS PO billing.
- Metered (usage-based) — flexible, aligns with variable consumption, slightly higher unit cost; good when usage growth is uncertain.
- Hybrid (baseline commitment + overage metered) — middle ground for predictable baseline spend with upside flexibility.

Term length guidance: 12 / 24 / 36 months supported. 18 months is uncommon on Marketplace (some buyers request it) — we can implement as a custom contract off-marketplace, but that loses Marketplace purchase flow/quotas. Recommendation: align to 12 or 24 months to keep within Marketplace private-offer standard templates.

Buyer approval gating (seller perspective):
- Small deals (< $50k ARR): often procurement + finance review only — ~3-7 business days.
- Mid deals ($50k–$250k): procurement + legal + finance + budget owner — ~7–21 business days.
- Large/enterprise (> $250k): procurement + legal + CIO/security + exec signoff — 3–8 weeks typical.

AWS Marketplace specific notes:
- Private offer creation by seller takes 1 business day; buyer acceptance + marketplace processing can take 1–5 business days.
- DocuSign flow or AWS acceptance: buyer must be an approved marketplace purchaser (billing/contracting status).

Simple decision tree (pasteable):
1) Identify estimated ARR and term -> 2) If ARR < $50k -> standard PO path (procurement + finance) -> target 1 week;
   else if ARR 50k–250k -> add legal review -> target 2 weeks;
   else -> engage sales leader + legal/exec -> target 3–6 weeks and consider cadence with AE for exec brief.

Actions I suggest:
- We prepare 2 private-offer templates for Skyline: (A) 12mo committed with 10% discount; (B) hybrid 12mo baseline + metered overage with 5% discount.
- Ask Skyline procurement to share the internal approval matrix (we received your flow — thanks).
- I'll loop Neha in to confirm Marketplace billing and any co-sell approvals needed.

I'll attach a one-pager (PO_Term_Scenarios.pdf) and a draft approval matrix (Approval_Matrix.xlsx) for you to share.

Ava — quick notes from the seller ops side that you can paste into the matrix: 
- Co-sell approval: for deals with expected ARR > $150k, flag for co-sell early (we'll need an ISV co-sell intake in SFDC and AWS partner team alignment). That adds ~3 business days to get partner ops sign-off but unlocks seller incentives.
- Marketplace PO tip: ensure Skyline's AWS account is registered and billing contact matches the PO to avoid acceptance delays.
- Legal redlines: we usually push for 60-day payment terms to align with Marketplace; if buyer insists on 90–120 days, run by finance for risk acceptance.

Amy — short answers and next steps:

- 18-month term: Marketplace does not natively support odd terms but you can do a staged structure: 12mo private offer (Marketplace) + pre-authorized 6mo renewal at agreed pricing. Operational caveat: the 6mo renewal would ideally be a Marketplace amendment or a follow-on PO — we recommend documenting the renewal trigger and pricing in your internal approval packet so finance/legal can sign off in advance.

- Overage billing on Marketplace (hybrid): usage above baseline is billed as metered line items on the Marketplace invoice and flows through AWS billing. Skyline will see baseline committed SKU + metered SKU charges; monthly invoice details usage units and unit price, and AWS handles chargeback to your linked billing account.

Planned next steps:
1) I'll send two private-offer drafts (12mo committed with 10% off, and 12mo baseline + metered overage with 5% off) for you to review with procurement.
2) Marcus and Neha will validate co-sell eligibility and any finance policy considerations.
